subproblem.title: C¹ segment estimate |v(x) − v(y)| ≤ ‖x − y‖ ∫₀¹ ‖Dv((1 − t)y + tx)‖ dt
subproblem.statement: Let n ∈ ℕ, ℝⁿ := Euclid n = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), v : ℝⁿ → ℝ of class C¹ (ContDiff ℝ 1 v), and x, y ∈ ℝⁿ. Then |v(x) − v(y)| ≤ ‖x − y‖ · ∫_0^1 ‖Dv((1 − t)y + tx)‖ dt, where Dv(z) = fderiv ℝ v z with the operator norm and the integral is the interval integral from 0 to 1.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (v : Euclid n → ℝ) (x y : Euclid n), ContDiff ℝ 1 v → |v x - v y| ≤ ‖x - y‖ * ∫ t in (0 : ℝ)..1, ‖fderiv ℝ v ((1 - t) • y + t • x)‖
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 1 (segment estimate) of the parent proof. Here it is stated for all x, y ∈ ℝⁿ and without the diameter bound, which the consumer convex_poincare applies itself (‖x − y‖ ≤ d). The segment is parametrized as p(t) = (1 − t)y + tx, so p(0) = y and p(1) = x.

Notation. ℝⁿ := Euclid n = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n). Dv(z) := fderiv ℝ v z ∈ L(ℝⁿ, ℝ), with the operator norm. ∫_0^1 is the interval integral.

1. Regularity. v is C¹ (ContDiff ℝ 1 v with 1 ≠ 0). So v is differentiable at every point, HasFDerivAt v (Dv(z)) z holds for all z, and z ↦ Dv(z) is continuous.
2. The segment. Let p(t) := (1 − t)y + tx for t ∈ ℝ. Then p is continuous, p(0) = y and p(1) = x. Its derivative at every t is (−1)·y + 1·x = x − y.
3. Chain rule. γ(t) := v(p(t)) has derivative γ'(t) = Dv(p(t))(x − y) at every t ∈ ℝ (HasFDerivAt.comp_hasDerivAt). The map t ↦ γ'(t) is continuous, since it is the continuous map t ↦ Dv(p(t)) evaluated at the fixed vector x − y. Hence γ' is interval integrable on [0, 1].
4. Fundamental theorem of calculus. ∫_0^1 γ'(t) dt = γ(1) − γ(0) = v(x) − v(y) (intervalIntegral.integral_eq_sub_of_hasDerivAt).
5. Since 0 ≤ 1, |v(x) − v(y)| = |∫_0^1 γ'(t) dt| ≤ ∫_0^1 |γ'(t)| dt (intervalIntegral.norm_integral_le_integral_norm).
6. For every t, |γ'(t)| = |Dv(p(t))(x − y)| ≤ ‖Dv(p(t))‖·‖x − y‖ = ‖x − y‖·‖Dv(p(t))‖ (operator-norm bound ContinuousLinearMap.le_opNorm). Both sides are continuous in t, hence interval integrable on [0, 1]. By monotonicity of the interval integral on [0, 1] (intervalIntegral.integral_mono_on),
   ∫_0^1 |γ'(t)| dt ≤ ∫_0^1 ‖x − y‖·‖Dv(p(t))‖ dt = ‖x − y‖·∫_0^1 ‖Dv(p(t))‖ dt
   (intervalIntegral.integral_const_mul).
7. Steps 5 and 6 give |v(x) − v(y)| ≤ ‖x − y‖·∫_0^1 ‖Dv((1 − t)y + tx)‖ dt. ∎

theorem Submission.cmcdt_cbm_sp_segment_bound : ∀ (n : ℕ) (v : Euclid n → ℝ) (x y : Euclid n), ContDiff ℝ 1 v → |v x - v y| ≤ ‖x - y‖ * ∫ t in (0 : ℝ)..1, ‖fderiv ℝ v ((1 - t) • y + t • x)‖ := by
  intro n v x y hv
  have hdiff : Differentiable ℝ v := hv.differentiable one_ne_zero
  have hcont : Continuous (fderiv ℝ v) := hv.continuous_fderiv one_ne_zero
  obtain ⟨p, hp⟩ : ∃ p : ℝ → Euclid n, p = fun t => (1 - t) • y + t • x := ⟨_, rfl⟩
  have hpc : Continuous p := by rw [hp]; fun_prop
  have hpd : ∀ t, HasDerivAt p (x - y) t := by
    intro t
    have h1 : HasDerivAt (fun t : ℝ => (1 - t) • y) ((-1 : ℝ) • y) t :=
      ((hasDerivAt_id t).const_sub 1).smul_const y
    have h2 : HasDerivAt (fun t : ℝ => t • x) ((1 : ℝ) • x) t := (hasDerivAt_id t).smul_const x
    have h3 := h1.add h2
    rw [hp]
    convert h3 using 1
    simp only [neg_smul, one_smul]
    abel
  have hγ : ∀ t, HasDerivAt (fun t => v (p t)) (fderiv ℝ v (p t) (x - y)) t := fun t =>
    (hdiff (p t)).hasFDerivAt.comp_hasDerivAt t (hpd t)
  have hγc : Continuous fun t => fderiv ℝ v (p t) (x - y) :=
    (hcont.comp hpc).clm_apply continuous_const
  have hftc : ∫ t in (0 : ℝ)..1, fderiv ℝ v (p t) (x - y) = v x - v y := by
    rw [intervalIntegral.integral_eq_sub_of_hasDerivAt (fun t _ => hγ t)
      (hγc.intervalIntegrable 0 1)]
    simp [hp]
  have hpt : ∀ t, (1 - t) • y + t • x = p t := fun t => by rw [hp]
  simp only [hpt]
  rw [← hftc, ← Real.norm_eq_abs]
  calc ‖∫ t in (0 : ℝ)..1, fderiv ℝ v (p t) (x - y)‖
      ≤ ∫ t in (0 : ℝ)..1, ‖fderiv ℝ v (p t) (x - y)‖ :=
        intervalIntegral.norm_integral_le_integral_norm zero_le_one
    _ ≤ ∫ t in (0 : ℝ)..1, ‖x - y‖ * ‖fderiv ℝ v (p t)‖ := by
        apply intervalIntegral.integral_mono_on zero_le_one
        · exact hγc.norm.intervalIntegrable 0 1
        · exact (continuous_const.mul (hcont.comp hpc).norm).intervalIntegrable 0 1
        · intro t _
          rw [mul_comm]
          exact (fderiv ℝ v (p t)).le_opNorm (x - y)
    _ = ‖x - y‖ * ∫ t in (0 : ℝ)..1, ‖fderiv ℝ v (p t)‖ :=
        intervalIntegral.integral_const_mul _ _
proof_key_steps: v ∈ C¹: v is differentiable everywhere and Dv is continuous.
p(t) = (1 − t)y + tx has p′ = x − y, p(0) = y, p(1) = x; by the chain rule (v∘p)′(t) = Dv(p(t))(x − y), which is continuous in t.
FTC: v(x) − v(y) = ∫_0^1 Dv(p(t))(x − y) dt.
